derivation_rule: Stage 2 derives an expectation per estate fact: a fact whose class is OBSERVE (all hops OBSERVE for a path) should appear in ACT's answer; a fact with any NOT_OBSERVE hop yields a truthful absence to be verified as such; PARTIALLY_OBSERVE applies its precondition; ENFORCE/REFUSE are effect-verified. No entry here is an expected ACT output.

entries.applies_to: agents with origin_category=NATIVE (ACT runs them)
entries.justification: A native agent is created through ACT's own registry; its existence is ACT's own record.

entries.applies_to: external agents listed by a configured HTTP registry discovery source (inventory_status=SHADOW_DISCOVERABLE or REGISTERED_IN_ACT)
entries.evidence_source: discovery_sources -> HTTP_AGENT_REGISTRY adapter -> discovery_observations -> ReconciliationService CREATE (control_state DISCOVERED)
entries.justification: Discovery is source-driven evidence: the adapter fetches the registry's list, each item becomes an append-only observation, and reconciliation derives a DISCOVERED agent.
entries.precondition: a DiscoverySource for that registry is configured in the tenant and a sweep runs; the registry is a real service (REAL_EXTERNAL_SERVICE_REQUIRED_STAGE2)

entries.applies_to: external agents listed by the cloud inventory (Bedrock Agents) source
entries.justification: The V7.5 adapter discovers exactly Bedrock AgentSummary constructs; existence of a listed agent is observable evidence once a source exists.
entries.precondition: a source with a read-only credential is configured; Stage 2 supplies the inventory service (mock or sandbox); the adapter is present only on the validation stack (ADR-0024, unmerged)

entries.applies_to: dark shadow agents (inventory_status=SHADOW_DARK: no discovery source lists them)
entries.justification: An agent that no configured source lists produces no observation; there is no evidence source that could reach it.
entries.missing_evidence: ACT has no network/process scanning; discovery is strictly source-driven and the fixed adapter registry has exactly two adapters

entries.applies_to: accountable owners of agents known to ACT
entries.evidence_source: agents.owner_id / owner_type / technical_owner_id / compliance_owner_id (+ posture rule no_accountable_owner for absence)
entries.justification: Ownership is a first-class column set; its absence is itself observable and evaluated by a posture rule.

entries.applies_to: the enterprise's actual owner of an agent ACT has not discovered or that was discovered but never claimed
entries.justification: For a DISCOVERED row ACT can state 'unowned in ACT'; it cannot observe who actually operates the process.
entries.missing_evidence: no evidence source carries enterprise ownership for a discovered agent; ownership enters ACT only through claim (AgentControlStateService) or registration

entries.applies_to: lifecycle_status of NATIVE agents
entries.justification: ACT owns the lifecycle of the agents it runs.

entries.applies_to: the enterprise's approval/lifecycle state of an external process
entries.justification: ACT's lifecycle column is ACT's record; nothing reads the external operator's approval state.
entries.missing_evidence: agents.lifecycle_status records ACT's registry state for the row, not the external system's own approval workflow; no ingestion of external approval state exists

entries.applies_to: origin_category / origin_provider
entries.evidence_source: agents.origin_category (CHECK NATIVE/EXTERNAL/UNKNOWN) and the soft origin_provider vocabulary; discovered agents carry the adapter's origin_provider
entries.justification: Category and provider are observable; the estate's finer 'provenance_quality' (documented/partial/unknown) has no field and collapses to the category.
entries.precondition: provenance quality beyond 'which adapter reported it' is not modelled; UNKNOWN is the truthful value when no source attests provenance

entries.applies_to: credentials ACT holds (tool_credentials, provider_credentials, connector_credentials) and agent API keys
entries.evidence_source: tool_credentials / provider_credentials / connector_credentials rows; posture rules stale_credential, expired_credential_still_active, dormant_agent_with_active_credential
entries.justification: Staleness/expiry of ACT-held credentials is evaluated by deterministic posture rules over ACT's own rows.

entries.applies_to: credentials held OUTSIDE ACT (shared service accounts, personal tokens used by external or dark processes) and their over-privilege
entries.justification: Posture rules read ACT-held credential rows only; the cloud adapter lists agents, not IAM policies (one action, bedrock:ListAgents).
entries.missing_evidence: no inventory of external credentials and no IAM/role ingestion exists; the estate's credential.posture for held_in_act=false has no ACT counterpart

entries.applies_to: tools registered in ACT and an agent's declared dependency on them
entries.evidence_source: tools rows + DEPENDS_ON_TOOL edges; posture rules unapproved_tool, excessive_tool_scope, dangerous_dependency
entries.justification: Tool approval and scope are ACT records; the dependency edge makes the relationship evaluable.

entries.applies_to: MCP servers registered in ACT (via the Tool domain) and DEPENDS_ON_MCP_SERVER edges
entries.justification: ADR-0018: an MCP server is a first-class row; its trust status and an agent's declared dependency are evaluable.

entries.applies_to: MCP use by an external process that was never declared or derived as an edge
entries.justification: Without an edge there is no fact in ACT; the graph never renders an absence as 'no dependency' (unknown != safe), but it cannot see the undeclared one either.
entries.missing_evidence: dependency edges are DECLARED by an operator or DERIVED from ACT's own execution rows (build_for_agent); no runtime MCP traffic of an external process is observed

entries.applies_to: agent -> tool/MCP/credential -> resource paths and their blast radius
entries.evidence_source: control_graph_edges (DEPENDENCY_EDGE_TYPES) walked by traverse_with_edges; blast radius returns incomplete=true at the depth cap, never a false 'empty'
entries.justification: Reachability is derived from recorded edges only; the estate's sensitive_reachability paths are observable exactly when each hop is an ACT edge.
entries.precondition: every hop must exist as a recorded edge (EXPLICIT/DERIVED/DISCOVERED) between nodes that resolve in the tenant; unrecorded hops are invisible (F5-3: blast radius is only as true as recorded edges)

entries.applies_to: sensitive resources as graph nodes
entries.evidence_source: resources rows (resource_type free text) as RESOURCE nodes
entries.justification: A resource is observable as a node; its sensitivity is not a resource attribute in ACT.
entries.precondition: ACT has no sensitivity classification on resources; 'RESTRICTED/CONFIDENTIAL' in the estate maps to agents.data_classification on the consuming agent, not to the resource

entries.applies_to: human -> human delegations
entries.evidence_source: delegations rows + DELEGATES_TO edges (create_delegation_edge); _delegation_prefix in authority-chain reconstruction
entries.justification: Human delegation is a recorded row with a producer.

entries.applies_to: agent -> agent authority (AGENT_DELEGATES_TO / TRUSTS between agents)
entries.justification: The edge type exists so ACT never has to invent it; nothing produces it, so the estate's agent_authority facts have no ACT counterpart until an operator declares them.
entries.missing_evidence: AGENT_DELEGATES_TO is declared in EDGE_TYPES but no code path creates such an edge (no producer, no ingestion); TRUSTS edges exist only when an operator declares them

entries.applies_to: actual runtime agent-to-agent handoffs (LangGraph state edges, CrewAI delegation, HTTP A2A calls)
entries.justification: V4/V7 measured 22 real handoffs -> 0 observed and 0 inferred; the absence is correct behaviour (no invented edge) and the boundary is the lack of any ingestion path.
entries.missing_evidence: no A2A protocol or framework-relationship ingestion; the gateway observes an agent's own boundary calls, never which peer caused them

entries.applies_to: persistent agent memory/context (what an agent remembers, where, for how long)
entries.justification: Nothing in ACT reads, stores or evaluates an agent's memory; a memory store that is also a RESOURCE node is observable only as a dependency edge if declared.
entries.missing_evidence: no table or model represents runtime memory or context state; the nearest field, agent_definitions.memory_requirements, is a declared requirement on a definition, not observed state

entries.applies_to: boundary calls (allowed and denied) by GATEWAY_ENFORCED external agents
entries.evidence_source: external_gateway_calls (one row per call: authz_decision, outcome, dispatch_status, grant, target)
entries.justification: Every signed call is recorded before dispatch; denial and allowance are both evidence.
entries.precondition: agent REGISTERED with external_enforcement_mode=GATEWAY_ENFORCED and a grant; the process is a real independent caller (ACTIVE_REAL_PROCESS_REQUIRED_STAGE2)

entries.applies_to: a call outside the grant's scope
entries.control_boundary: GatewayService.decide: identity.scoped_for(capability, target) -> DENY 'outside grant scope'; denied calls are never dispatched (DB CHECK ck_ext_calls_denied_never_dispatched)
entries.justification: Scope bounds but never grants; the denial is a real effect (no dispatch), verified in V4/V6/V7.

entries.applies_to: a threat finding for repeated denied boundary calls by a gateway-enforced agent
entries.justification: Enforcement is perfect and detection is silent for this agent class - a wiring gap (the data exists in external_gateway_calls), confirmed in V6 and felt in V7 (39 denials -> 0 findings).
entries.missing_evidence: all six threat rules read agent_executions / runtime_governance_decisions / tool_calls; none reads external_gateway_calls, and a gateway-enforced agent never produces an execution

entries.applies_to: a threat finding for repeated governance denials of a NATIVE agent
entries.evidence_source: threat rule governance_denial_spike over runtime_governance_decisions joined to agent_executions (threshold min_denials=3)
entries.justification: For ACT-run agents the execution rows exist and the rule fires deterministically.

entries.applies_to: an undiscovered process calling the gateway with a grant issued to another registered agent
entries.evidence_source: external_gateway_calls attribute the call to the grant's agent (key_id -> grant -> agent_id)
entries.justification: The call is observed and enforced, but attributed to the wrong (registered) agent - a credential-sharing fact the estate records objectively.
entries.precondition: ACT cannot distinguish the true caller from the grant's registered agent; the attribution is to the grant holder

entries.applies_to: suspending or terminating an external/discovered agent's process
entries.control_boundary: ContainmentOrchestrator.truthful_capability: performs only when control_state == 'GOVERNED'; every other agent gets status REFUSED with a refusal_reason and no effect (ADR-0020); GOVERNED is legal only for NATIVE (ADR-0023)
entries.justification: ACT does not run the process, so it cannot truthfully claim to stop it; the refusal is the correct, verified behaviour (V6: REFUSED, agent still live).

entries.applies_to: revoking an external agent's gateway grant
entries.control_boundary: ExternalGrantService.revoke sets revoked_at; ExternalGrantService.verify then rejects the key (EXTERNAL_GRANT_REVOKED, 403); revocation is uncached
entries.justification: This is authority ACT genuinely controls; V6/V7 verified the effect (subsequent calls 403, target silent).
entries.precondition: the agent holds a grant ACT issued

entries.applies_to: suspending a NATIVE GOVERNED agent
entries.control_boundary: containment SUSPEND_AGENT -> KillSwitchService (lifecycle_status SUSPENDED, active executions cancelled); requires explicit confirmation; not reversible by automation
entries.justification: ACT runs the agent, so the effect is real and effect-verified (V6).

entries.applies_to: declaring an EXTERNAL/UNKNOWN agent GOVERNED
entries.justification: The column cannot lie in either direction; an external agent tops out at REGISTERED.

entries.applies_to: a discovered identifier equal to a NATIVE agent's external_reference
entries.evidence_source: ReconciliationService: NATIVE collision always FLAGs a discovery_findings row (RECONCILIATION_AMBIGUOUS); never a silent merge
entries.justification: The conflict is surfaced as a human-review finding, deterministically.

entries.applies_to: a discovered agent that disappears from its source
entries.evidence_source: check_staleness -> STALE_AGENT finding, never a deletion; auto-resolved on re-observation
entries.justification: Staleness is observable and non-destructive; its precision depends on the sweep being complete.
entries.precondition: the sweep that misses it must be complete; a bounded/partial sweep evaluates staleness against a partial set (V9-5) and can flag agents that still exist

entries.applies_to: reachability over branching trust/delegation graphs at depth >= 16
entries.evidence_source: AuthorityChainService.reachability over control_graph_edges with a path-array cycle guard
entries.justification: The answer exists relationally (a frontier-dedup form returns it), but the shipped query shape cannot complete on dense graphs.
entries.precondition: the CTE enumerates simple paths, so cost is exponential in branching x depth; shallow or tree-like graphs answer, dense ones abort at the default depth (V9-1)

entries.applies_to: an authority chain for an action by an external agent
entries.justification: Attribution exists (grant -> agent -> issuer), but the 5.3 chain surface does not cover it.
entries.missing_evidence: reconstruct_authority_chain starts FROM agent_executions; gateway-enforced external agents produce none - their actions are attributed by grant and issuer, not by a reconstructed chain

entries.applies_to: any relationship, traversal or read across tenants
entries.control_boundary: organization_id on every domain table; per-hop organization_id predicate in every recursive CTE; cross-tenant nodes resolve to nothing (404-class refusal, no existence leak)
entries.justification: Verified at every rung in V5 and V9: hostile cross-tenant edges are truncated at the tenant edge.

entries.applies_to: well-governed agents (the control group)
entries.evidence_source: the 16 posture rules evaluate every agent; a healthy agent should produce no serious finding
entries.justification: Observability includes the absence of findings; Stage 2 measures specificity/false positives here.
